newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada churches ship food to Rwanda.
newsitem.headline: Canada churches ship food to Rwanda.

text.p: A Canadian church group said on Monday it has begun shipping the first of 9,000 tonnes in donated food to Rwandan refugees.
"There's a thousand tonnes in place now. The volume could go up after our board meeting in December and if the partners decide to give more," Canadian Foodgrains Bank spokeswoman Trish Jordan said.

The Winnipeg-based agency represents 13 Christian church groups and takes donations of grains and oilseeds from Canadian farmers. The agency focuses on Rwanda's refugees and the malnourished of North Korea, Afghanistan and Liberia.

Varying quantities of grain, lentils and oilseeds will be shipped to Rwanda's refugees via Kigali between now and May. The Canadian International Development Agency, a government body, did not plan to add to the food aid.
"The NGOs (non-governmental organisations) in the region have the supplies they need. It has not yet received our attention," CIDA spokesman Andre Desrosiers said.
Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale committed Canada week at the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organisation summit last week to donate 400,000 tonnes of food aid in the current fiscal year.
